Rashi on Nazir 3a:10:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא האי ושולח מים ריבוי הוא - דכי משקין ליה מיא לארעא, קא מרבי להו לפרי:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:10:1.english: And if you wish, say [that] this "and sends water" is an increase - For when one irrigates the land with water, it makes the produce grow.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:11:1.hebrew: ציפרין הסמוכין לשיער - והיכן הן ציפרין הסמוכין לשיער? כדכתיב בדניאל: ״עד די שעריה כנשרין רבה וטפרוהי כצפרין״ — דצפרין ושיער בחד קרא כתיבי:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:11:1.english: Birds that are juxtaposed to hair - And where are birds juxtaposed to hair? As it is written in Daniel: “Until his hair grew like eagles’ [feathers], and his nails like birds’ [claws]” — for birds and hair are written in a single verse.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:12:1.hebrew: דר"מ סבר מיתפיס איניש במידי דסמיך ליה - ולהכי אמר ״צפרין״, דבעי לקבולי עליה גידול שיער דסמיך ליה לצפורים. וכגון שהיה נזיר עובר לפניו או תפוס בשערו, כדאמרינן לעיל:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:12:1.english: For Rabbi Meir holds [that] a person associates [his vow] with something that is juxtaposed to it - And for this reason he said “birds” — because he wanted to accept upon himself the growing of hair, which is juxtaposed to birds. And [this is in a case] such as where a nazirite was passing before him, or he was holding his hair, as we said above.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:1.hebrew: אין דאפילו לרבי אלעזר הקפר דאמר נזיר חוטא - ולא מיקרי נאה, דכתיב: ״וכפר עליו מאשר חטא על הנפש״ (במדבר ו):
Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:1.english: Yes, for even according to Rabbi Elazar HaKappar, who said [that] a nazirite is a sinner - and [therefore] he is not called “beautiful,” as it is written: “And he shall make atonement for him, for that he sinned regarding the soul” (Numbers 6:11).

Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:2.hebrew: הני מילי גבי נזיר טמא - שנטמא, דאיידי דבעי מיסתר ימים הראשונים ומיהדר ומימני זימנא אחריתי, אריכא ליה מילתא:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:2.english: This applies to an impure nazirite - [One] who became impure; for since he must void the first days and return and count another time, the matter is prolonged for him.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:3.hebrew: דילמא אתי למיעבר על נזירותיה - כדאמר בפרק קמא דנדרים (דף ט:): כשהן מטמאין ורבין עליהם ימי טומאה, מתחרטין בהן, ונמצאו מביאין חולין לעזרה:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:3.english: Perhaps he will come to transgress his naziriteship - As it says in the first chapter of Nedarim (9b): “When they become impure and the days of impurity multiply upon them, they regret them [their vows], and it turns out that they bring unconsecrated [animals] into the Temple courtyard.”

Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:4.hebrew: אבל נזיר טהור לאו חוטא קרינא ביה - ואמרי': ״זיל ותיהוי נזיר והנאה״:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:1:4.english: However, [with regard to] a ritually pure nazirite, he is not called a sinner - And we say [to him]: “Go and be a nazirite, and [derive] benefit.”

Rashi on Nazir 3a:2:1.hebrew: נהי נמי - דמוקמת ליה כגון שתפוס בשערו, אמאי הוי נזיר? והא לא אמר "הריני כזה", דאי "כזה" אמר — הכי משמע להו: "הריני כזה שיער לגדלו":
Rashi on Nazir 3a:2:1.english: Though [this is] indeed - [Even] if you establish it [as a case] where he is holding his hair, why is he a nazirite? Behold, he did not say "I am hereby [a nazirite] like this" — for if he said "like this" [while holding his hair], this is what it implies to them: "I am hereby [undertaking to have] hair like this, to grow it."

Rashi on Nazir 3a:2:2.english: Shmuel said: For example, where a nazirite was passing before him - For it implies: "I am hereby in naziriteship like this [one]."

Rashi on Nazir 3a:3:1.hebrew: הריני מסלסל הריני מכלכל או שאמר הרי עלי לשלח פרע הרי זה נזיר - "הריני מסלסל" משמע — דליעביד מידי דליהוי מהפך בשערו בגידול, דהיינו בנזירות:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:3:1.english: "I am hereby curling [my hair], I am hereby growing [my hair]," or if he said: "It is incumbent upon me to let [my hair] grow long" — behold, he is a nazirite - [The phrase] "I am hereby curling" implies that he will do something so that he will be turning [i.e., curling] his hair through [its] growth, namely, in naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:4:1.hebrew: ואימא תורה - דכי אמר ״הריני מסלסל״ — שמקבל עליו ללמוד תורה, וקאמר שיהא מהפך בה, כדכתיב: ״סלסלה ותרוממך״:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:4:1.english: And say [it refers to] Torah - For when he said, "I am hereby curling," [say] that he is accepting upon himself to study Torah, and he is saying that he will turn it over [i.e., delve into it], as it is written: "Extol her and she will exalt you" (Proverbs 4:8).

Rashi on Nazir 3a:5:1.hebrew: כדתנן - המוציא סיד בשבת מרשות היחיד לרשות הרבים, שחייב משום ״לא תוציאו״:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:5:1.english: As we learned [in a mishna] - One who carries out lime on Shabbat from the private domain to the public domain, who is liable on account of "You shall not carry out."

Rashi on Nazir 3a:5:2.hebrew: כדי לסוד כילכול ואמר רב בת צידעא - טינפל"א (צדע, רקה) בלע"ז — שמקפל השער שברקתה כמין מגרר, כדי להעמיד על גבן כיפה שבראשה, שלא יפול השער שבאוזן למטה:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:5:2.english: Sufficient to smear a kilkul, and Rav said: The temple - temple (temple, side of the head) in Old French — where one folds the hair on her temple like a scraper, in order to set upon them the cap that is on her head, so that the hair at the ear will not fall down.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:6:1.english: And say [that he meant] to sustain the poor - He accepted [this] upon himself.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:7:1.english: “It is incumbent upon me to let long hair grow,” he is a nazirite - For it implies: “It is incumbent upon me to grow long hair.”

Rashi on Nazir 3a:7:2.hebrew: ממאי דהדין שילוח רבויא הוא - כדקאמרת, דלגדל פרע משמע:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:7:2.english: From where [is it known] that this shilu'aḥ is [an expression of] increase - As you said, that it means to grow long hair.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:7:3.english: As it is written: “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates” - Your shoots that grow will be like an orchard of pomegranates that sprouts and grows.

Rashi on Nazir 3a:8:1.hebrew: ואימא דשילוח מידי דעבורי - הוא דמשמע שיגוז שערו, כמפנה מים ומעבירן ממקום למקום, כדכתיב: ״ושולח מים וגו'״. והאי נמי דאמר ״הרי עלי לשלח פרע״, משמע דאמר: ״הרי עלי להעביר פרע״:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:8:1.english: And say that shilu'aḥ is a matter of removal - It means that he will shear his hair, like one who clears away water and moves it from place to place, as it is written: “And sends water...” etc. (Job 5:10). And this [person] too who said, “It is incumbent upon me to send [leshale'aḥ] long hair,” it implies that he said: “It is incumbent upon me to remove [my] long hair.”

Rashi on Nazir 3a:9:1.hebrew: תנא פרע פרע יליף כתיב הכא - בנזיר: ״גדל פרע״, וכתיב גבי כהן הדיוט: ״ופרע לא ישלחו״. מה פרע דכתיב גבי כהן הדיוט לישנא דריבוי הוא — כדאמרינן בפרק כ"ג (סנהדרין כב:): ״פרע ליהוי עד שלשים, ומירבא לא לירבי טפי משלשים״, דגמרינן ליה מנזיר, דכתיב ביה (במדבר ו) ״יהיה״, ו״יהיה״ בגימטריא הכי הוי — אף פרע האמור גבי נזיר גידול שיער הוי, והכי משמע: שיניחנו לגדל עד שיבא לכלל פרע, שהן שלשים. ואפילו בעי למימר דלעולם שילוח מידי דעבר הוא — אכתי לא קשיא ולא מידי, דהכי משמע: ״הרי עלי לשלח שיער (ולהביאו שיגיע) לכלל ל' שיהא פרע״, דבין פרע דנזיר ובין פרע דכהן הדיוט אינה פחותה משלשים:
Rashi on Nazir 3a:9:1.english: The Tanna derives [by verbal analogy] pera [from] pera; it is written here - Regarding a nazirite, [it is written]: "[he shall let] the locks grow" [gadel pera], and it is written regarding an ordinary priest: "and locks they shall not let grow" [u'pera lo yeshaleḥu]. Just as pera that is written regarding an ordinary priest is an expression of growth — as we say in the chapter [entitled] 'Kohen Gadol' (Sanhedrin 22b): "Let there be pera up to thirty [days], and let him not grow [his hair] more than thirty [days]," for we derive it from a nazirite, about whom it is written (Numbers 6[:5]): "he shall be [yihye]," and yihye in gematria is this [thirty] — so too, the pera stated regarding a nazirite is hair growth, and this is what it means: that he shall let it grow until it reaches the status of pera, which is thirty [days]. And even if one should wish to say that shilu'aḥ is always a matter of passing [along] — still there is no difficulty whatsoever, for this is what it means: "Behold, it is incumbent upon me to extend the hair (and bring it so that it will reach) the status of thirty [days], so that it will be pera," as neither the pera of a nazirite nor the pera of an ordinary priest is less than thirty [days].

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:10:1.hebrew: משקין ליה מיא לפרי ורבי - פירוש: גדל הפרי. וקשה, דאשכחן הרבה שילוח שאינו לשון גידול אלא לשון העברה, כמו "שלח תשלח" (דברים כ״ב:ז׳), "וישלח יעקב מלאכים" (בראשית ל״ב:ד׳). ויש לומר, דאי תותבי' מהנך קראי, הוה משני ליה כדלעיל: "תנא 'פרע' 'פרע' יליף", ולא בא לפרש אלא למקרא דאותבינן מיניה: "ושולח מים". ודוחק, דמשמע דהניח הג"ש מכל וכל, ועתה אינו צריך לה כלל. לכן נ"ל, דמתחילה לא היה חושש רק שימצא לו פסוק אחד דמשמע לשון רביה, וקמייתי ליה מקרא ד"שלחיך". ודחי ליה הש"ס: דלמא ההוא גופיה לשון העברה, כמו "ושולח מים", וליכא אפילו חד קרא דלשתמע לשון רבויא. ואהא משני: "איבעית אימא, האי שולח מים לשון רבוי הוא", ואיכא למילף מיניה, או מקרא ד"שלחיך פרדס". ואע"ג דקראי טובא לשון העברה, שפיר ילפינן מחד קרא דהוי לשון רבויא, דמסתברא דעתו אנזירות הוא:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:10:1.english: "One waters produce with water, and it grows" - Explanation: the produce grows. And [this] is difficult: for we find many [instances of] shilu'aḥ that are not an expression of growth, but rather an expression of dispatch, such as: "You shall surely send away [the mother]" (Deuteronomy 22:7), and "And Jacob sent messengers" (Genesis 32:4). And one could say: that if one were to challenge him from those verses, he would have answered him as above: "The Tanna derives [it from the verbal analogy of] pera [and] pera"; and he only came to explain the verse from which we objected: "And sends water." Yet [this explanation] is forced, because [the formulation "And if you wish, say"] implies that he abandoned the gezerah shavah entirely, and now has no need for it at all. Therefore, it seems to me: that from the outset, he was only concerned with finding a single verse that implies an expression of increase, and he brought it from the verse "Your shoots [shelaḥayikh]" (Song of Songs 4:13). And the Gemara rejected this: perhaps that [verse] itself is an expression of transfer, like "And sends water", and there is not even a single verse that can be understood as an expression of increase! And to this it answers: "If you wish, say that this 'sends water' is an expression of increase," and one can derive [it] from it, or from the verse "Your shoots are an orchard [of pomegranates]." And even though many verses are an expression of transfer, we can well derive from a single verse that it is an expression of increase, for it is reasonable [to assume that] his intention was for naziriteship.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:11:1.hebrew: צפורים הסמוכין לשיער קיבל עליה - האמורין בפסוק אצל שער. כלומר: אע"פ דאמר "צפורים" סתמא — דהא מתני' סתמא קאמר — אפילו הכי סבירא ליה לריש לקיש דדעתיה דאיניש אצפורים הסמוכים לשיער. והכי משתמע ליה: האומר "הרי עלי צפורים" הרי זה נזיר, דכיון דצפורים סמוכין לשיער קאמר, מסתמא ה"ק: "הרי עלי מצוה דשייכא ביה צפורין התלויה במצות שיער", דהיינו נזיר, שאם נטמא צריך צפורין; וה"פ: מצוה התלויה בצפורין. אכן אין לפרש משום סמיכות גרידא כדמפרש הש"ס, דאם כן, "הרי עלי נשרין" הל"ל דהוי נזיר, דטפי סמיכי לשער:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:11:1.english: "Birds that are juxtaposed to hair he accepted upon himself" - [This refers to the birds] mentioned in the verse next to hair. That is to say: even though he said "birds" without qualification — for the Mishnah states [it] without qualification — nevertheless, Reish Lakish holds that a person's intention is toward the birds that are juxtaposed to hair. And this is how [Reish Lakish] understands [the Mishnah]: One who says, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] birds," is a nazirite, because since he meant birds that are juxtaposed to hair, presumably this is what he is saying: "Incumbent upon me is the mitzvah involving birds which depends on the mitzvah of hair" — namely, a nazirite, for if he becomes ritually impure, he requires birds; and this is the explanation [of his words]: "[Incumbent upon me is] a mitzvah that depends on birds." However, one should not explain [that he becomes a nazirite] due to juxtaposition alone, as [a simple reading of] the Gemara explains; for if so, [the Mishnah] should have said [that if one says,] "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] eagles," he is a nazirite, since they are even closer [in the verse] to hair.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:11:2.english: "Until his hair grew like eagles' [feathers], and his nails like birds' [claws]" - This is a verse in Daniel regarding Nebuchadnezzar.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:2:1.hebrew: הריני כזה נהי נמי דתפיס בשערו הרי נזיר - יש ספרים דכתיב בהן: "הריני כזה לא אמר", אכן טעות הוא, שהרי במתני' תני בהדיא: אמר "הריני כזה". ושמא הסופר טעה במאי דכתב בתר הכי: "אמר שמואל: בשנזיר כו'". פי': דס"ד דאין נזיר עובר לפניו, אלא דתפיס בשעריה, דומיא דמתני' דלעיל "אהא נאה" דאוקמינן בתפיס בשעריה לחוד. ולכך פריך: "הריני כזה" לא משמע מידי דנזירות, אף על גב דתפיס בשעריה. ומשני שמואל: הכא נמי כשנזיר עובר לפניו, והשתא אין צריך לומר דתפיס בשעריה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:2:1.english: "I am hereby like this" — Granted that he is holding his hair, "Behold, [I am] a nazirite" - There are books in which it is written: "He did not say: 'I am hereby like this.'" However, this is an error, for in the Mishnah it is taught explicitly: [He] said, "I am hereby like this." And perhaps the scribe erred because of what is written after this: "Shmuel said: Where a nazirite etc." Explanation: For one might have thought that a nazirite was not passing before him, but rather that he was holding his hair, similar to the Mishnah above, "I will be beautiful," which we established as [referring to] holding his hair alone. And therefore [the Gemara] challenges: "I am hereby like this" does not imply anything of naziriteship, even though he is holding his hair. And Shmuel resolves: Here, too, [it is a case] where a nazirite was passing before him. And now, it is not necessary to say that he is holding his hair.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:3:1.hebrew: ממאי דהדין סילסול שערא הוא - דלשון זה נופל אהפוך שיער, דנימא נזירות קביל עליה? ואימא תורה — להפך בתורה:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:3:1.english: "From where [is it known] that this silsul is hair?" - For does this expression apply to the curling [literally, turning] of hair, such that we should say he accepted naziriteship upon himself? Say rather [that it refers to] Torah — to delve [literally, turn over] in Torah.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:4:1.hebrew: הכא נמי תפוס בשעריה - דמשמע שפיר: הריני מהפך במצוה התלויה בשיער:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:4:1.english: "Here too, he is holding his hair" - For it clearly means: "I am hereby engaging in a mitzvah that depends on hair" [i.e., naziriteship].

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:7:1.hebrew: שילוח רבוי הוא - לשון גידול, כמו "שלחיך פרדס רמונים". ו"אימא מידי דעבורי הוא" — שקיבל עליו לגלח ולהעביר השיער לכשיגדל:
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:7:1.english: "Shilu’aḥ is an increase" - [It is] an expression of growth, as in "Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates." And [as for the objection,] "Say that it is a matter of removal" — [this means] that he accepted upon himself to shave and remove the hair once it grows.

Tosafot on Nazir 3a:9:1.hebrew: תנא פרע פרע יליף - לאו אתנא דמתני' קאי, אלא אתנא דסנהדרין (דף כב:), דקאמר: כהן הדיוט צריך לגלח אחת לשלשים יום, ויליף "פרע לא ישלחו" מנזיר, דכתיב "גדל פרע" — מה להלן שלשים יום, כמנין "יהיה", אף בכהן הדיוט שלשים יום; וקאמר "לא ישלחו". והכא הכי פירושא: תנא "פרע" "פרע" יליף בעלמא, אלמא דשילוח הוי לשון גידול. ואם תאמר: ולייתי מקרא דכתיב בכהן הדיוט, "ופרע לא ישלחו", ואכתי ג"ש למה לי? ונראה לי, דמקרא דכהן הדיוט לא משמע ד"לא ישלחו" הוי גידול אפילו דתרי יומי, וכיון דלא אמר בפירוש "הריני נזיר תרי יומי", אלא "שילוח פרע", אין כאן קבלת נזירות. אבל כי גמרינן כהן הדיוט מנזיר, דשילוח הוי מלשון שלשים בג"ש, וקאמר "הרי [עלי] לשלח", כאילו אמר "הרי עלי לשלח פרע שלשים יום", ומשתמע שפיר דנזירות קביל עליה — להכי מייתי ג"ש. ודווקא כי אמר "הרי עלי לשלח פרע", אבל אמר "הרי עלי פרע" בלא שילוח — לא משמע מידי, דפרע הויא לשון גילוי, כמו "ופרע ראש האשה" (במדבר ה׳:י״ח):
Tosafot on Nazir 3a:9:1.english: The tanna derives [from] "pera" [and] "pera" - This does not refer to the tanna of our Mishnah; rather, [it refers] to the tanna in Sanhedrin (22b), who says: A common priest must cut his hair once every thirty days, and he derives "they shall not let their locks grow long" from a nazirite, as it is written: "he shall let the locks grow" — just as there [regarding a nazirite, it is] thirty days, corresponding to the numerical value of "yihyeh", so too regarding a common priest [it is] thirty days; and [the verse] says: "they shall not let [their locks] grow long." And here, this is the explanation: The tanna elsewhere derives [via the verbal analogy of] "pera" [and] "pera," from which it is evident that "shilu’aḥ" is an expression of growth. And if you say: Then let [the Gemara] cite [directly] from the verse written regarding a common priest, "and they shall not let their locks grow long," and why do I still need a gezeirah shavah? And it appears to me that from the verse of a common priest, it does not imply that "they shall not let [their locks] grow long" is growth of [more than] even two days; and since he did not explicitly say, "I am hereby a nazirite for two days," but rather "growth of locks [shilu’aḥ pera]," there is no acceptance of naziriteship here. But when we learn [the law of] a common priest from a nazirite via a gezeirah shavah, that "shilu’aḥ" is an expression of thirty [days], and he says, "It is [incumbent upon me] to grow [locks]," it is as though he said, "It is incumbent upon me to grow long locks for thirty days," and it is well understood that he accepted naziriteship upon himself — for this reason, [the Gemara] cites the gezeirah shavah. And [he is a nazirite] specifically when he says, "It is incumbent upon me to grow long locks [pera]"; but if he said, "It is incumbent upon me [to have] pera" without [the word] "shilu’aḥ," it does not mean anything, as pera is an expression of uncovering, as in: "and he shall uncover the woman’s head" (Numbers 5:18).
